_readme: THIS IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR YOUR HARDWARE AND ENDPOINTS.
Describe each machine you own once, list what is installed on it, and run
`npm run inventory:sync`. That regenerates every consumer config:
Do not hand-edit those files — your edits will be overwritten and CI will fail.

cloudEscalation.note: Cloud is strictly opt-in. While optIn is false, routing and fallback never select cloud hosts, even when every self-hosted lane is unreachable. Set optIn to true or export XX_STACK_ALLOW_CLOUD=1 to enable it.

limits: Best for low-latency coding and iterative execution
Do not schedule many concurrent heavy reasoning jobs while actively developing
If multiple slices need different Ollama models here, serialize them and switch only at explicit handoff boundaries

runtimes.notes: Enable if you run llama-server locally on :8080.

network.notes: REPLACE `address` with your own machine's MagicDNS name — `gpu-rig` is a placeholder, not a resolvable host. Reached over Tailscale by MagicDNS name. Do not expose these ports publicly; bind them to the tailnet interface (find it with `tailscale ip -4` on the rig) or firewall them to the tailnet.

limits: Primary lane runs sglang on :30000; keep Ollama as the compatibility lane
Prefer the sglang lane for long-context and high-throughput work

runtimes.notes: Preferred remote lane. sglang batches concurrent requests across the GPUs, so parallel slices are close to free relative to sequential execution.

Ollama binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and is not reachable over Tailscale until you set OLLAMA_HOST on the rig and restart it. Enable this runtime once that is done and `ollama list` shows the model below.

aggregators.label: Hermes local-first control plane (loopback proxy)
aggregators.notes: OpenAI-compatible loopback proxy exposed by hermes-orchestration. Start it with `python3 hermes-orchestration/scripts/hermes_orchestrator.py serve` and export HERMES_PROXY_TOKEN. Hermes applies its own lane policy behind this single endpoint, so enabling it delegates lane selection to Hermes instead of routing to a backend directly. Leave disabled if you would rather address your machines directly — the two approaches are alternatives, not layers.

models.name: hermes-auto
models.notes: Virtual model name — Hermes resolves the real backend per its own lane policy.

providers.label: Generic OpenAI-compatible cloud endpoint
providers.notes: Template. Replace endpoint and models with a real provider if you opt in to cloud.

providers.label: Google Gemini
providers.notes: Template. Requires an API key; only reachable when cloud escalation is opted in.

hermesCli.notes: Hermes reaches this through the local `hermes` CLI rather than an HTTP endpoint. Still gated by policy.cloudEscalation.optIn on the xx-stack side and by --allow-cloud on the Hermes side.
